record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Does last-passage percolation with general weight distributions exhibit the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling, including the correct fluctuation and correlation exponents?

evidence.quote: In particular showing that LPP with general weights has 3 : 2 : 1 scaling, is far from being resolved.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider directed last-passage percolation on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$ defined as follows. Let $\{w(i,j) : (i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2\}$ be a family of i.i.d. nonnegative random variables with common distribution $F$ (the "weights"). For $(m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$, define the last-passage time
$$ L(m,n) \;=\; \max_{\pi:(0,0)\to(m,n)} \sum_{(i,j)\in\pi} w(i,j), $$
where the maximum is taken over all up-right lattice paths $\pi$ from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$ (i.e. paths that at each step increase exactly one coordinate by $1$).

The Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality conjecture predicts the following "3:2:1" scaling behaviour for $L$. There exist a deterministic constant $\mu = \mu(F) > 0$ (the time constant in the direction $(1,1)$) and constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that:

(i) Fluctuation exponent $1/3$: as $N \to \infty$,
$$ \frac{L(N,N) - \mu N}{c_1 N^{1/3}} \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathrm{TW}_{\mathrm{GUE}}, $$
where $\mathrm{TW}_{\mathrm{GUE}}$ denotes the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution.

(ii) Transversal/correlation exponent $2/3$: the typical transversal fluctuations of the maximising path from $(0,0)$ to $(N,N)$ are of order $N^{2/3}$, and on the spatial scale $N^{2/3}$ the rescaled fluctuation field converges (in an appropriate sense) to the Airy$_2$ process; equivalently, with $t$ playing the role of the longitudinal coordinate, the scaled process
$$ \frac{L(N + \lfloor c_2 x N^{2/3}\rfloor,\, N - \lfloor c_2 x N^{2/3}\rfloor) - \mu_x N}{c_1 N^{1/3}} $$
converges as $N\to\infty$ to the Airy$_2$ process in $x$ (minus a parabola), reflecting the 3:2:1 scaling of fluctuation:transversal:longitudinal coordinates.

Question. Does (i)–(ii) hold for last-passage percolation with general weight distributions $F$? More precisely, identify a natural class of weight distributions $F$ (for example, all continuous distributions with sufficiently many moments and no atom at the top of the support) for which one can prove that $L$ exhibits the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling described above, with the Tracy–Widom GUE one-point limit and the Airy$_2$ correlation structure.
artifact.status_search_result: KPZ universality with full 3:2:1 scaling for last-passage percolation is rigorously established only for special integrable weight distributions (notably exponential and geometric). For general weights the conjecture remains widely cited as a central open problem; recent work (e.g. convex upper bounds, hierarchical environments, partial universality results for tilted/perturbed integrable models) makes partial progress but does not resolve the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: KPZ Universality: Scaling & Fluctuation Insights
status_evidence.snippet: KPZ class fluctuations persist when the distribution of weights is no longer exponential ... is a very compelling and entirely open problem; the only other solvable case is geometric weights.
status_evidence.claim: Universality of KPZ fluctuations in LPP beyond exponential/geometric weights is described as an entirely open problem.

status_evidence.title: Last passage percolation in hierarchical environments
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work examines power-law tail weights as a critical case for KPZ scaling relations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research addresses partial universality questions but does not establish 3:2:1 scaling for general weights.

status_evidence.title: KPZ limit theorems (Baik, ICM)
status_evidence.snippet: The KPZ fixed point is conjectured as the universal 3:2:1 scaling limit, proved only for integrable models.
status_evidence.claim: Full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling for general LPP remains conjectural.
